title: Authorization anchor and surgical privilege model for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a composable RBAC v2 model built around the concepts of an 'authorization anchor' and 'surgical privileges' to enable least-privilege by default, scoped delegations, and high-fidelity audit trails. This ticket captures the role and resource hierarchy, a compact permission grid, decision rules for implicit vs explicit grants/denies, and how audit context should propagate for elevated sessions (breakglass/timebound elevations). The goal is a design that is compatible with Redwood Private (VPC) restrictions, Dedicated-admin workflows, and Console RBAC controls.
acceptance_criteria: A clearly documented role anchor concept that maps one or more anchor roles to resource-tenancy boundaries
Permission grammar and compact matrix for common resource types (Model, Deployment, Project, Billing, Org) with examples
Surgical privilege primitives defined: timebox, scope-exchange, delegated-temporary-role, and explicit-deny override
Audit context plan: event fields, session linkage, and elevation provenance captured in logs
Migration path from current RBAC v1 datasets with a safe rollout plan (canary + audit-only mode)
decisions: Anchor model: every tenant has 0..N anchors (e.g., org-admin, infra-anchor) which act as scopes for role resolution
Default deny: implicit deny by default; only explicit allow rules are surfaced in runtime evaluation cache
Elevations are timebound tokens which must include executor, reason, and parent-session id for auditability
Deny precedence: explicit deny always overrides allow, including on delegated temporary roles
Permission inheritance limited to parent->child resource edges; no automatic lateral inheritance across unrelated resources
design_notes: Authorization anchor is a lightweight namespace — not a full role; it simplifies cross-tenant delegation semantics
Surgical privileges are modeled as capability tokens attached to a session rather than permanent bindings on a principal
We will represent permissions using a triple: <action>:<resource-type>:<resource-pattern> and permit wildcards only at template edges
KV cache keys for permission checks should include anchor id + principal id + timebox hash to allow fast invalidation when elevations expire
Plan to expose a Console UI that shows explainer traces for a permission decision (why allowed/denied), backed by the evaluation log
permission_matrix_summary: Core resource types and example permissions: Model (model.read, model.deploy, model.manage), Deployment (deployment.invoke, deployment.scale, deployment.manage), Project (project.read, project.edit, project.manage), Billing (billing.view, billing.pay, billing.manage), Org (org.read, org.manage). Anchor-bound roles map to permission bundles (e.g., 'anchor-deployer' => [model.deploy, deployment.invoke]). Surgical privileges grant a minimal action set for a bounded time and are audited as separate events.
migration_strategy: Phase 1: Schema extension - add anchor_id and elevation_token columns to current role bindings (audit-only writes enabled)
Phase 2: Permission evaluator dual-run (v1 behavior + v2 behavior) with divergence logging for 2 weeks
Phase 3: Rollout - enable v2 enforcement for Canary tenant group; gather metrics on false-deny/false-allow
Phase 4: Gradual rollout with opt-out toggle in Console and final cutover after policy reconciliations
